SddCritic.keywords: critic, orchestrator, spec-review, task-review, blind-spot, multi-round, reconcile, surgical-edit, sdd-critic
SddCritic.Mission:
Autonomous critique loop for one SDD review-set. I am the ORCHESTRATOR and sole owner of its edit/re-dispatch loop: each round dispatches one isolated read-only sensor, evaluates findings in project context, reconciles introduced entities via `orient`, edits only the manifest-derived write-set, and re-dispatches after edits. Five rounds are automatic; crossing each active cap needs an operator decision. One primary keeps the shared `## Critic Rounds` until readiness; secondary members never duplicate it. Apply every `MECHANICAL` edit directly; the round checkpoint asks only about unresolved `GOAL` findings (`AX_GOAL_OWNER_GATE`). Severity never creates a confirm-after-fix Ask. The sensor only reports; only the operator downgrades a `GOAL` tag.
A separate skill (`/sdd-critic`). Input — a spec / task / bounded bundle target. Output — the reviewed bundle + the final verdict.
SddCritic.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED, HALT_FORMAT, SESSION_FILE_FORMAT
Orchestrator owns artifact, applies edits. Critic is sensor — reports only, never edits.
Critic receives ONLY the canonical bounded target-set (a decomposed scope plus all its module specs, or one complete standalone artifact set) and the minimal parent/neighbourhood slices required by the protocol. Confusion = underspecification. Fix the artifact bundle.
The dispatched critic runs on a model no stronger than the artifact's author — default the worker tier (Sonnet-class), never a step up "to be thorough". The consumers of a spec are workers on cheap models; a spec that only a stronger model can parse is not fit for execution (`AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` carried from narrative text into tooling). The `understanding` and `implementation-autonomy` lenses ARE the weak model's strength — it surfaces exactly what a worker would trip on. Semantic depth beyond that is not the critic's job; it stays with external review.
Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.
Introducing a parallel mechanism where an existing one from a neighbour spec could be extended is a decision at GOAL level, never a silent author call. "Вводим новое" is a valid answer ONLY when it names the specific neighbour invariant / requirement ID the existing mechanism cannot satisfy, and records the choice as its own Decision Log entry (`DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`) citing that ID. No cited ID, no entry → the mechanism stays unjustified: route it back to the operator as an open question, not a decision already made on their behalf. This governs the AUTHOR's system-fit check (`STEP_*_SYSTEM_FIT` in `scope` / `module` / `interface` / `infra`); `AX_REUSE_FIRST` runs the same bias against duplication from the CRITIC's reactive vantage, after the artifact already exists — the two apply one belief at two different points in the lifecycle, not two competing rules.
Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `-DL-N — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.
Close the gap only. No restructure, rewrite, restyle. Structural overhaul → suggest re-scaffold, stop.
Uncertain → ACCEPT. Cost of rejecting real finding > cost of accepting marginal one.
Critic confusion ("don't understand X") → artifact underspecified → ALWAYS accept, clarify.
Every finding carries an addressee — who owns its resolution: - `MECHANICAL` — style, structure, consistency, a detail the spec already implies. Resolved by an artifact edit. - `GOAL` — goal / scope shift ("goal drawn too narrow"), misunderstood intent, a missing requirement, an unanswered uncomfortable question. Resolved ONLY by the goal owner — the operator.
A finding that removes or weakens an existing quality gate — typecheck, lint, format, or tests run from a hook, script, or CI — or steps back from an infra axiom's stated default, is `GOAL` by definition, never `MECHANICAL`, no matter how small the edit looks. The operator owns the tradeoff between gate strength and friction; the answer is recorded as its own Decision Log entry (`AX_GOAL_OWNER_GATE`).
The operator owns the goal. A `GOAL` finding is resolved by an operator answer, and the edit follows the answer — `AX_DEFAULT_ACCEPT` covers `MECHANICAL` findings only. The sensor's `GOAL` tag stands until an operator answer says otherwise — downgrading it to `MECHANICAL` is the operator's call alone; an orchestrator that reads a `GOAL`-tagged finding as mechanical carries that disagreement into the SAME question block as one more question, never a private reclassification. Batch the round's `GOAL` findings into ONE question block (`QUESTION_FORMAT`) BEFORE editing the sections they touch. Goal / scope wording stays intact until an operator answer sanctions the change.
The sole no-Ask resolution is an answer the operator accepted previously and whose durable source (a Decision Log id or an exact prior operator-decision record) is cited; it applies only while the present question and consequences are unchanged. Every other `GOAL` is new and enters that one batched Ask before any related edit. Calling it low-risk, a default, or intent-preserving never turns a new `GOAL` into a mechanical decision.
When the resolved `GOAL` finding weakened or removed a quality gate (`AX_FINDING_ADDRESSEE`), the operator's answer is written as its own Decision Log entry, not folded into the round's edit summary — a gate change is a standing decision that future rounds, and future sessions, must be able to see without replaying this round's dialogue.
CRITICAL — unusable, downstream agent produces wrong work. MAJOR — gap requiring rework. MINOR — improvement, vague wording. INFO — observation.
Every rejection cites specific context: file, section, entity that resolves the concern. No vague "more context."
Any edit → another isolated post-edit review dispatch mandatory, no exception of the agent's own making — "the fix is trivial" does not waive it; edits may create contradictions detectable only by a post-edit sensor pass. Whether a dispatch continues an existing worker or starts a fresh one belongs to the owning review step, not this global rule. The verdict handed to the operator MUST be the literal verdict text of the LAST dispatch actually run, shown as a direct quote — never a paraphrase, and never the verdict of a dispatch that was skipped.
Zero edits → stop. Unchanged input → unchanged verdict → infinite loop.
Five critic results is the hard automatic cap. At the fifth result — regardless of sensor verdict — the operator must dispose the cycle before readiness or another dispatch. If that round made no edits, the choices are `CLEAN`, `CONTINUE THROUGH ROUND N` with an explicit higher cap, or `RESTART: reason`; if it made edits, CLEAN is unavailable because the changed bytes have not been reviewed, so only CONTINUE or RESTART are offered. A raised cap behaves identically when reached. The sensor cannot authorize continuation, and continuation is never readiness.
`## Critic Rounds` is memory that lives in exactly ONE primary artifact for the canonical target-set, not in the orchestrator's own context and not duplicated into secondary bundle members. It survives a context reset, a crashed session, or a fresh fallback sensor that never saw a prior round. Append-only inside one stable review-set/write-set cycle: each round adds one dated entry (verdict, target-set, write-set, changed-state, dispatch disposition, accepted, rejected-with-reason, reconcile decisions, changes, out-of-cycle deferrals, and any operator decision); a prior entry is never rewritten. This makes the critique loop converge across rounds and sessions: the sensor reads the primary history together with every bounded target artifact, so settled ground is not re-litigated. Keep the block through `npx gennady sdd-check --review-ready ` and exact `npx gennady sdd-check --review-publication [secondary...]`. An integrated lifecycle retains it through semantic-finalization corrections and the final delta-only operator disposition; those corrections continue the same numbered cycle and cannot reset the five-result cap. Remove scratch only as the last review-scaffolding mutation after final bytes are stable and accepted; no artifact edit may follow. A direct critic pause/continuation retains it too. A changed target-set or promoted write-set starts a new Round 1 cycle rather than appending incompatible evidence. Continuation authorization is not readiness.
Tasks critiqued in DAG layers. Same layer (no inter-dependencies) → parallel dispatch. Different layers → sequential.

SessionState.Contract:
The primary artifact's `## Critic Rounds` remains the canonical completed-round history. Between a sensor return and that completed entry, the compatible SDD session journal is the durable pending state. Persist one compact JSON line with schema `sdd-critic-sensor/v1`, cycle target/write-set hashes, `resultCount` (the next Round number), Changed-state, literal sensor verdict, literal findings, reconciled addressees, and dispatch disposition. Write it to the regular non-symlink `.claude/tmp/sdd-critic-event.json`, then run the current transition's exact critic-event ToolCall. Tool success is mandatory BEFORE any artifact edit, GOAL/cap Ask, CLEAN decision, or redispatch; inline free text is forbidden.
Every operator answer is a separate later immutable event in the same schema, with `event=goal-disposition` or `event=cap-disposition`, the referenced `resultCount`, and the exact answer. Append it before applying the answer. After STEP_3C completes the primary's canonical Round entry, append `event=round-recorded`. On resume, fold the matching session events against the artifact history: a sensor result lacking a required disposition re-presents the recorded Ask and never redispatches/increments; a disposition lacking `round-recorded` resumes the remaining edit / record transition. This fold occurs in STEP_0 before the dispatch step; the pending branch skips dispatch/evaluate/persist and resumes the first incomplete edit/disposition/record transition. A recorded round permits the next dispatch. A changed target/write-set appends `event=cycle-restarted` before beginning new Round 1. Session close performs final scratch cleanup.

SddCritic.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_ARTIFACT` | The target spec / task does not exist | | `H_PARENT_SPEC_MISSING` | A task's parent spec is missing — cannot critique a task without its spec | | `H_DISPATCH_FAILED` | The sensor subagent failed to dispatch twice — surface to the operator, do not loop silently | | `H_CRITIC_NOT_READY` | `npx gennady sdd-check --review-ready ` fails while evidence still exists — do not finalize or remove it | | `H_CRITIC_PUBLICATION_INVALID` | `npx gennady sdd-check --review-publication [secondary...]` cannot derive one exact role-validated publication-set from the critic's spec-only write-set plus bounded durable outputs — do not remove scratch or publish | | `H_GOAL_BLOCKED` | `GOAL` findings block the round and the operator is unavailable to answer — stop, report the pending question block |

Step.Action:
Resolve one canonical ordered review-set, its one primary artifact, and the non-empty write-set derived by `sdd-check --review-state` from valid `CHANGE_MANIFEST` sections. Spec review is scope-local: a decomposed product/library scope is primary with ALL its declared module specs; cross-scope neighbours are bounded context, never members of this history. Infrastructure/interface may be standalone. A task batch remains DAG-layered per `AX_TASK_PARALLEL`. Missing → `H_NO_ARTIFACT`. If an existing cycle names another review-set or write-set, start a fresh Round 1 with reason `target-set changed: ` or `write-set changed: `; never continue across either identity.
Before STEP_1, fold matching `CRITIC_SENSOR_STATE_FORMAT` events against the primary's completed `## Critic Rounds`. An unrecorded `sensor-result` is `resumePendingResult`: skip STEP_1_DISPATCH through STEP_2C_PERSIST_SENSOR and resume the first incomplete STEP_3 → STEP_3C transition. A required disposition that is absent re-presents the Ask from the persisted result; an existing disposition is applied without asking again. Neither path redispatches, increments, or resets the pending result. Only no pending result may enter STEP_1.

Step.Goal: Clear the FLOW_VERSION/READINESS preflight gate before dispatching the sensor.
Step.Action: Use `FLOW_VERSION`, `AUTHORING_READY`, `EXECUTION_READY`, and `GATE_QUEUE` from the already-gathered `sdd-state` snapshot; do not enter task lifecycle merely to clear this gate. Size the gate to this request's own blast radius (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`). The router already applied the shared readiness gate before loading this directive; do not repeat or reinterpret it here.

Enter only when STEP_0 found no `resumePendingResult`. Immediately before EVERY dispatch, run exact reviewState ToolCall below; retain its Target-set, Write-set, and Changed-state in this round. The sensor always reads the full review-set and receives the exact current session `glossary:` list as read-only input. Round 1 is fresh. For a later round over the SAME review-set/write-set, continue that SAME worker/session when supported, sending the changed-set plus explicit confirmation that the full target-set is unchanged and the write-set is unchanged. Record `Dispatch: continued`. A fresh fallback is allowed only when continuation is unsupported, the session was lost, or the sensor failed; send the full review-set and record `fresh — continuation unavailable: `, `fresh — session lost: `, or `fresh — session failed: `. Never invoke a nested agent CLI to simulate continuation. Use a worker-tier model (`AX_CRITIC_MODEL_TIER`); every handoff names primary, round, protocol, sets, Changed-state, and saved glossary. Emit one `ORCHESTRATOR_PROGRESS_FORMAT` line. npx gennady sdd-check --review-state [secondary...] Inputs , [secondary...]: =canonical primary resolved in STEP_0; [secondary...]=same ordered remaining review-set from STEP_0. Use reviewState.

Step.Goal: Weigh findings against full project context.
Step.Action:
Split by addressee (`AX_FINDING_ADDRESSEE`): `MECHANICAL` — accept by default (`AX_DEFAULT_ACCEPT`); `GOAL` — queue for STEP_3B (`AX_GOAL_OWNER_GATE`). Parse the sensor's final `GlossarySuggestions` field per `SESSION_FILE_FORMAT`; deduplicate it against the saved glossary and carry genuinely new/conflicting items to the next existing operator checkpoint, never a glossary-only Ask. A finding that requires changing a read-only review-set member cannot enter this cycle's edit set: either route it as a blocker to that artifact's authoring owner, or promote the member by adding a valid manifest and RESTART with `write-set changed: `. Never edit it silently. A rejection cites a specific resolving file/section (`AX_REJECTION_REASON`). Sensor confusion the full context resolves = artifact bug (`AX_CONFUSION_BUG`); project ambiguity = `GOAL`. Carry severity (`AX_SEVERITY`); weakening a quality gate is always `GOAL`.
Convergence brake from round 3 on: a NEW finding (not already carried in a prior `## Critic Rounds` entry) advances to STEP_3 / STEP_3B only if `CRITICAL`, or a regression — a defect a prior round's own edit introduced. A new `MINOR` / `MAJOR` finding that is neither stays out of this cycle's edit set — record it in this round's entry under `Out of cycle:` and carry it into the STEP_5 report as its own list, never silently dropped (AUTHORING.md §9 — a stop needs a named outlet, not a bare refusal).

Step.Goal: Walk the graph from the artifact to the portal; reconcile every entity the WHOLE artifact introduces, not only this round's findings. (mechanical → tool)
Step.Action: Run exact orientation ToolCall below once for EACH artifact in the bounded target-set — one hop from that artifact to its portal, declared-dependency neighbours, and consumers; this is the ORCHESTRATOR's own step, on full project context, not a widening of the sensor's bounded read (`AX_ISOLATION_SIGNAL` still governs STEP_1_DISPATCH). The sweep is proactive over EVERY entity/contract/mechanism the bundle introduces, never narrowed to only the entities this round's findings happen to name — a duplicate the sensor never flagged is still a duplicate. For each: reuse > extend > justify > escalate (`AX_REUSE_FIRST`); "justify" requires the specific neighbour invariant/requirement ID the existing mechanism could not satisfy, recorded as its own Decision Log entry (`AX_PARALLEL_MECHANISM_REQUIRES_JUSTIFICATION`, `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`). Two outcomes route to `GOAL`, never a silent `MECHANICAL` fix: (1) the artifact duplicates a mechanism the `sdd-orient` extract already names on a neighbour, (2) the artifact's introduced entity conflicts with a neighbour requirement the extract surfaces. Do not let the critique invent a duplicate of an existing entity. npx gennady sdd-orient Inputs : =each literal Target-set member returned by STEP_1, one separate call per member. Use orientation.

Step.Goal: Make the returned sensor result and cumulative count durable before any decision or edit.
Step.Action: Set `resultCount` to the next canonical Round number and append the exact `sensor-result` event through `CRITIC_SENSOR_STATE_FORMAT`; require criticEvent success. This transition occurs after addressee/reconcile classification but BEFORE STEP_3, every GOAL/cap Ask, CLEAN/proceed, or another dispatch. On resume, consume a matching pending event rather than dispatching the sensor again; never increment a recorded result twice. npx gennady sdd-session log --content-file .claude/tmp/sdd-critic-event.json Payload: exact sensor-result event. Use criticSensorEvent before STEP_3.

Edit only write-set members and only what a finding requires (`AX_SURGICAL`); I apply edits — the sensor never does (`AX_OWNER`). Apply every `MECHANICAL` finding directly (`AX_DEFAULT_ACCEPT`) regardless of severity; severity does not create an extra confirmation. Leave `GOAL` sections untouched until the operator answers. Record the round's edits once at STEP_3C.

Step.Goal: One batch Ask per round for every operator-owned item (`AX_GOAL_OWNER_GATE`).
Step.Action: Resolve every `GOAL` finding against accepted operator decisions and the Decision Log first. Auto-resolution is allowed only when the same answer was previously accepted by the operator, still applies with unchanged consequences, and is cited by its Decision Log id or exact prior operator-decision record. Every other `GOAL` is new — regardless of low risk, an apparent default, or preserved product intent — and enters the batch before any related edit. Its question names the consequence that makes it new or reopens it. Build ONE `AskUserQuestion` batch (`QUESTION_FORMAT` batching rule — independent questions ride together) carrying every remaining new `GOAL` fork from STEP_2 or STEP_2B as its own question, including any orchestrator disagreement with a sensor's `GOAL` tag («critic tagged GOAL, I read this as mechanical because …») — the tag stands until this answer says otherwise. A `CRITICAL` / `MAJOR` mechanical finding never creates a separate confirm-after-edit Ask. When no unresolved `GOAL` exists → skip the Ask, go straight to STEP_3C (`AX_DEFAULT_ACCEPT`). WAIT for the answer before touching any `GOAL`-tagged section. Before applying an answer, append its separate immutable `goal-disposition` event for this `resultCount` and require criticEvent success. Apply `GOAL` edits exactly as answered, and any correction the operator makes to a confirmed fix — recorded together at STEP_3C, not here. When this checkpoint or `H_GOAL_BLOCKED` waits for the operator, return `TerminalDecision: pause` and preserve the SDD session; an unresolved Ask is never completion. When the answered `GOAL` finding weakened or removed a quality gate, additionally write the operator's decision as its own Decision Log entry (`AX_GOAL_OWNER_GATE`). Any accepted glossary item sharing this checkpoint is persisted with the inherited router glossaryUpdate before reuse. Operator unreachable while `GOAL` findings block → `H_GOAL_BLOCKED`. npx gennady sdd-session log --content-file .claude/tmp/sdd-critic-event.json Payload: exact goal-disposition event. Use criticGoalDispositionEvent before applying the answer.

Step.Goal: At the active automatic cap, obtain the operator's explicit disposition before another dispatch (`AX_CAP_5`).
Step.Action: Rounds before the active cap skip this step. At Round 5 — and at every operator-raised cap — Ask regardless of sensor verdict. If `Changes: none`, offer exactly: (a) operator CLEAN; (b) continue through an explicitly named higher cap `CONTINUE THROUGH ROUND `; (c) correct target/approach and `RESTART: `. If this round edited any write-set member, CLEAN is unavailable because those bytes have not had a subsequent sensor pass; offer only CONTINUE or RESTART. Before applying the exact answer, append its separate immutable `cap-disposition` event for this `resultCount` and require criticEvent success. CLEAN keeps the sensor verdict honest and permits readiness without another dispatch; CONTINUE permits only rounds through the new cap; RESTART ends this cycle, applies the correction, recomputes review-state, and starts a fresh Round 1. While this cap decision is unanswered, return `TerminalDecision: pause` and preserve the session. The sensor cannot authorize a sixth round. Never rewrite its verdict into `OPERATOR_ACCEPTED`. npx gennady sdd-session log --content-file .claude/tmp/sdd-critic-event.json Payload: exact cap-disposition event. Use criticCapDispositionEvent before applying the answer.

Step.Goal: Append this round's memory to the artifact (`AX_SCRATCH_LOG`).
Step.Action:
Append ONE entry to `## Critic Rounds` in the one primary artifact only — create the section at the end of that artifact on Round 1; secondary target artifacts never receive a copy. Never rewrite a prior entry; this block is append-only:
``` ### Round — - Verdict: - Target-set: - Write-set: - Changed-state: - Dispatch: - Accepted: — - Rejected: — "" → - Reconcile: <entity → REUSE | EXTEND | JUSTIFY | ESCALATE> - Changes: - Out of cycle: - Operator-decision: # only when STEP_3B2 asked ```
`Accepted` covers both the `MECHANICAL` edits applied at STEP_3 and the `GOAL` edits applied at STEP_3B after the operator's answer. `Rejected` carries the exact reason per `AX_REJECTION_REASON` — a later round, or a later session picking this up fresh, reads this entry before re-raising the same ground. Even on a CLEAN round this entry is appended before STEP_5 runs readiness; the block must still exist when the command validates it (`AX_SCRATCH_LOG`). After this canonical entry is durable, append `round-recorded` through `CRITIC_SENSOR_STATE_FORMAT`. A context resume consumes the pending sensor/disposition events and finishes this step without redispatching or incrementing the result. npx gennady sdd-session log --content-file .claude/tmp/sdd-critic-event.json Payload: exact round-recorded event. Use criticRoundRecordedEvent before STEP_4.

Before the active cap: CLEAN with `Changes: none` → STEP_5; any edits → another dispatch (`AX_RE_DISPATCH`) whose STEP_1 `reviewState.Changed-state` must differ; zero edits with a non-clean verdict → stop not-ready and never dispatch another round (`AX_STOP_NO_EDITS`). At the cap: operator CLEAN is valid only with `Changes: none` and goes to STEP_5 without another dispatch; CONTINUE raises the cap and continues; RESTART returns to STEP_0 as a fresh cycle. No automatic dispatch crosses the cap (`AX_CAP_5`).

While the primary's `## Critic Rounds` still exists, run exactly projectFeasibility ToolCall below before reviewReadiness. A project-feasibility finding means the reviewed specs have inconsistent declared rows or artifact ownership: return it to the owning scope/infra external-dependencies audit and do not finalize a scope-local CLEAN. A GREEN result is structural evidence only; this critic still owns the semantic judgement that the specs are jointly executable. Then run exactly reviewReadiness ToolCall below. Failure → `H_CRITIC_NOT_READY`. Then run exact reviewPublication ToolCall below with the same ordered spec arguments used by review-state; failure → `H_CRITIC_PUBLICATION_INVALID`. Retain and return its literal `target-set`, spec-only `write-set`, role-bearing JSON `publication-set`, and `publication-state`; auxiliary publication members never enter critic ownership. Keep `## Critic Rounds` intact: the review lifecycle removes it only after semantic finalization, the final delta-only operator disposition, and the last publication recheck. Report the literal final sensor verdict (CLEAN | NEEDS_WORK | CRITICAL), the separate operator decision when present, and a one-line-per-round summary, plus merged `Out of cycle` findings and the retained publication output. The verdict MUST be the literal verdict of the LAST sensor dispatch actually run (`AX_RE_DISPATCH`), never a paraphrase and never replaced by operator CLEAN. A structural problem the critique cannot resolve surgically → escalate, do not loop.
When review-lifecycle dispatched this critic, return `TerminalDecision: continue` with the saved publication output and retained scratch to that already-loaded caller; internal review handoff never closes the session. For a forced direct `critic` entry, render the terminal menu per `NEXT_STEP_MENU_FORMAT`: continuing into review-lifecycle returns `continue`, pause returns `pause`, and only after this step establishes `unfinished chained work: none` may literal «Complete / finish» removes scratch only after revalidating the unchanged publication output, then returns `TerminalDecision: complete` and runs exact terminal ToolCall below once. The decision source is this STEP_5 direct-entry menu, never CLEAN or a successful check. A pause or continuation keeps scratch. npx gennady sdd-check --project-feasibility Use projectFeasibility before reviewReadiness.npx gennady sdd-check --review-ready Inputs : =primary artifact path resolved in STEP_0 whose Critic Rounds embeds the frozen bundle. Use reviewReadiness.npx gennady sdd-check --review-publication [secondary...] Inputs , [secondary...]: and [secondary...]=same ordered spec arguments frozen by STEP_1 review-state. Use reviewPublication.npx gennady sdd-session close

ChatOutput.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words, without numbering and without semantic question IDs; under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name; skipping the explanation and firing a bare list of options is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
Пример — иллюстрация формата, не задание:
### 💡 Куда положить ресёрч-документ Документ можно держать рядом со спекой — виден в контексте скоупа, проще найти, пока читаешь её — или в общем каталоге ресёрчей, если он пригодится за пределами одного скоупа; для разового ресёрча под конкретную спеку разница небольшая. ✅ **Рядом со спекой** `[specs//research/]` — виден в контексте скоупа, не потеряется. Иначе: - **Общий каталог** `[docs/research/]` — _за: виден без привязки к одному скоупу · против: сложнее понять, к какой спеке относится_
(AskUserQuestion: «Рядом со спекой (рекомендую)» · «Общий каталог»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
Пример — иллюстрация формата, не задание:
### 💡 Граница нового скоупа Функциональность можно оформить отдельным скоупом или модулем внутри существующего — от этого зависит, где заводить спеку и как считать её границы; пре-анкоринг здесь дороже, чем в низкоставочном случае. - **Отдельный скоуп** `[new-scope]` — _за: чистая граница, не тащит чужие инварианты · против: больше координации между скоупами_ - **Модуль внутри существующего скоупа** `[module-in-scope]` — _за: меньше накладных расходов, общий контекст уже есть · против: граница скоупа расползается со временем_ - **Отложить решение до следующей итерации** `[defer]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск закрепить границу раньше, чем видно реальное использование

A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:

A counter-question in reply to a gate is a side-dive, not a rejection: (a) answer the counter-question in full, on its own merits, before returning to the gate; (b) bring the gate back exactly once, marked as a repeat pass, enriched with whatever the counter-question surfaced — «повторяю вопрос» plus a fact or option the side-dive added (e.g. operator asked "как ты делаешь ресёрч?" → the repeat pass adds an option «сначала ресёрч, потом решаем»); a verbatim repeat of the first gate carries no delta and is itself the violation. (c) if the operator answers the repeat pass with another counter-question instead of a pick, do not fire a third pass — stop and ask directly what is blocking the decision.
